recipe: Allocate the majority of your testing effort to integration tests rather than unit tests, as they verify that different parts of your application work together correctly.
trigger_condition: When deciding how to distribute testing effort across a React application's test suite.
evidence: It's crucial to focus on integration tests for most of your testing, as they provide significant benefits and boost confidence in your application's reliability.

recipe: Write component tests that verify user-facing behavior rather than internal implementation details, so tests remain valid after refactoring.
trigger_condition: When writing tests for React components using Testing Library.
evidence: Its philosophy is to test your app in a way it is being used by a real world user instead of testing implementation details.

recipe: Assert on what a component renders to the user instead of checking internal state values, so your tests survive state management refactors.
trigger_condition: When writing component tests and deciding which assertions to make.
evidence: For example, don't test what is the current state value in a component, but test what that component renders on the screen for its user.

recipe: Run Playwright e2e tests in browser mode locally for development and in headless mode in your CI/CD pipeline on every deploy.
trigger_condition: When setting up e2e test execution for a React application.
evidence: Browser mode - it will open a dedicated browser and run your application from start to finish. You get a nice set of tools to visualize and inspect your application on each step. Since this is a more expensive option, you want to run it only locally when developing the application.

recipe: Use MSW to define mocked API handlers when you only have frontend access and the backend features you need aren't implemented yet, so you can build and test frontend features without hardcoding response data.
trigger_condition: When you only have access to the frontend and are blocked by unimplemented backend features.
evidence: This is especially useful if you only have access to the frontend and are blocked by some not implemented features on the backend.

recipe: Instead of mocking fetch calls in your tests, set up a fully functional mocked API server via MSW and make real HTTP requests to it with the data your application expects.
trigger_condition: When writing integration tests that require API responses.
evidence: Having a fully functional mocked API server is also handy when it comes to testing, you don't have to mock fetch, but make requests to the mocked server instead with the data your application would expect.

recipe: Reserve unit tests for shared components and functions used throughout the application, or for complex logic isolated within a single component.
trigger_condition: When deciding which parts of your application to cover with unit tests.
evidence: They are useful for testing shared components and functions that are used throughout the entire application. They are also useful for testing complex logic in a single component.

recipe: Ensure your tests remain relevant after refactoring to a different state management solution by focusing on the component's output to the user rather than internal state.
trigger_condition: When refactoring a React application to use a different state management solution.
evidence: If you refactor your app to use a different state management solution for example, the tests should still be relevant as the actual component output to the user shouldn't change.
